text: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD as long as Jehoiada the priest lived.
Jehoiada found two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.
Some time later Joash resolved to restore the house of the LORD.

He gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the towns of Judah and collect money from all Israel, year by year, to repair the house of your God. See that you act quickly in this matter." But the Levites did not act quickly.

So the king summoned Jehoiada the chief priest and said to him, "Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax laid down by Moses, the servant of the LORD, and by the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?"
For the sons of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into the house of God and had even used all its sacred objects for the Baals.
At the king's command they made a chest and placed it outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.
Then a proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem that the tax imposed on Israel in the wilderness by Moses, the servant of God, should be brought to the LORD.
All the officials and all the people rejoiced; they brought their contributions and dropped them into the chest until it was full.

Whenever the chest was carried by the Levites to the king's officers and they saw that there was a great deal of money in it, the king's secretary and the chief priest's officer would come, empty the chest, and carry it back to its place. This they did day after day, and they collected a large amount of money.

The king and Jehoiada handed it over to those who carried out the work of the house of the LORD, and they hired stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair it.
The workmen labored, and under their hands the work of repair went forward. They restored the house of God according to its original design and reinforced it.

When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, and it was used to make utensils for the house of the LORD: vessels for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and articles of gold and silver. And throughout Jehoiada's lifetime burnt offerings were presented continually in the house of the LORD.
Jehoiada grew old and full of years, and he died at the age of a hundred and thirty.
They buried him in the City of David with the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God and toward his house.
After the death of Jehoiada, the officials of Judah came and bowed before the king, and he listened to them.
They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherah poles and the idols. Because of this guilt of theirs, wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem.
The LORD sent prophets among them to bring them back to himself; they testified against them, but the people would not listen.

Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood above the people and said to them, "This is what God says: Why do you break the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, he has forsaken you."

versions.text: Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood before the people and said to them, "This is what God says: Why do you break the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, he has forsaken you."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מֵעַל לָעָם means "above the people" (from a raised position, likely in the temple court), which pictures a public, authoritative proclamation. "Before the people" loses this spatial nuance and flattens the image.

text: But they conspired against him, and at the king's command they stoned him to death in the courtyard of the house of the LORD.
King Joash did not remember the kindness that Jehoiada his father had shown him, but killed Jehoiada's son. As he lay dying he said, "May the LORD see this and call you to account."

versions.text: King Joash did not remember the kindness that Zechariah's father Jehoiada had shown him, but killed his son. As he lay dying he said, "May the LORD see this and call you to account."
versions.explanation: In Hebrew "his father" describes Jehoiada's fatherly role toward Joash, not toward Zechariah; the current wording shifts the relationship and weakens the moral irony (Joash killed the son of the man who had been a father to him). Naming Jehoiada in the second clause keeps the referent clear for hearers.

text: At the turn of the year the army of Aram marched against Joash. They invaded Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed all the leaders of the people, and sent all the plunder to the king of Damascus.

Though the army of Aram had come with only a few men, the LORD delivered into their hands a very great army, because Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers. So they carried out judgment on Joash.

When the Arameans withdrew, they left him severely wounded. His own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed. So he died, and they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

versions.text: When the Arameans withdrew, they left him severely wounded. His own servants conspired against him for the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed. So he died, and they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "the sons of Jehoiada" (plural). If the singular is retained for clarity (referring to Zechariah), a brief footnote noting the plural in the Hebrew would help; otherwise the plural should be represented.

text: Those who conspired against him were Zabad, son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad, son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
The account of his sons, the many prophecies against him, and the restoration of the house of God are written in the commentary on the Book of the Kings. And Amaziah his son succeeded him as king.
